title: LVM-MO: A Large Vision Model Pioneer on Full-Chip Mask Optimization
problem: Full-chip mask optimization (MO) challenges in post-Moore era require handling entire layouts with optical proximity and process bias effects; existing clip-level restoration approaches exhibit limited correction, poor generalization, and inefficiency at full-chip scale.
motivation: Extending resolution enhancement techniques is pivotal for post-Moore semiconductor manufacturing; full-chip MO must balance correction fidelity with computational efficiency.
method: Proposes data-driven large vision model (foundation model) for full-chip mask optimization with a layout feature extractor aware of polygon mutual influence in long-range pattern perception, optical physics, and lithography chemistry; treats MO as a vision task enabling learning across diverse mask patterns.
key_novelty: Foundation large vision model for full-chip mask optimization with lithography-aware layout feature extraction, enabling high-fidelity full-chip scale processing.
contributions: Data-driven large vision model for mask optimization
Lithography-aware layout feature extractor modeling polygon interdependencies
Foundation model trained on massive lithography dataset
Improved resolution fidelity, correction speed, and full-chip scalability vs SOTA

metrics.other: resolution fidelity, correction speed, full-chip scalability improvements

limitations: Not discussed; focus is on scalability and accuracy gains.
primary_theme: Large vision model for full-chip lithography mask optimization
